newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch gas exploration up, 1997 promising - Woodmac.
newsitem.headline: Dutch gas exploration up, 1997 promising - Woodmac.

text.p: Dutch gas exploration has increased markedly this year and the prospects for 1997 are good as companies target Dutch satellite fields, says industry analyst Wood Mackenzie in its latest Northwest Europe report.

"Exploration and appraisal activity on the Dutch shelf has increased dramatically during 1996, compared with 1995 levels. This has been accompanied by an increase in success rate, albeit mainly in established areas," Woodmac said in its November report published on Thursday.
Twenty-three offshore exploration wells have been completed so far this year, versus 10 in 1995, with a success rate of 58 percent. Most discoveries were satellite fields in established areas.
Onshore, six wells have been completed, three of them successful, Woodmac said.
Capital expenditure was expected to peak in 1997 at about 2.2 billion guilders ($1.3 billion), from 1.6 billion ($1.0 billion) in 1995.
"The encouraging exploration success rate and recent acreage awards mean that the outlook for exploration and appraisal activity in 197 remains bright," the report said.
The successful wells have raised Dutch gas reserves by 2.3 TCF (trillion cubic feet) since the start of 1995, and, in the next two years, Dutch gas reserves could rise by 7.2 TCF.
"21 new offshore fields, with reserves of 3.5 TCF, and around 18 new onshore gas fields, with reserves of 3.7 TCF, could be producing by the end of the century," the report said.

Dutch gas output is set to increase by 12 percent from 7.6 bcfd (billion cubic feet per day) to a peak of 8.5 bcfd in 1998 with a rise in supply from Groningen and from new developments in North Friesland.
